LoginRequest.description:
Login, deliberately without the registration rules.

Two reasons, both learned the hard way. `dev@fdip.local` is a reserved TLD
that `EmailStr` refuses, so the seeded account could never log in. And more
generally, tightening the registration policy must never lock out an account
that already exists: a login is authenticated by lookup, not by format.
LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest

PasswordChange.description:
The current password is required even though the session proves identity.

A session can be borrowed — a shared screen, a stolen cookie. Requiring the
current password means taking the account permanently needs more than
sitting down at someone's desk.
PasswordChange.title: PasswordChange

PatchVersion.description:
Level 1 edits to a draft version. Fields and custom fields are replaced
wholesale, because a partial merge of a field map is ambiguous.

TestRunProblem.description:
One required field that was not found, and what to do about it.

A failed run that only says "did not pass" leaves a customer guessing. There
are exactly two things they can do — pick documents that contain the field,
or make it optional — so the message says both.
TestRunProblem.title: TestRunProblem

get.description:
What has happened on this project: uploads, corrections, decisions,
exports, key changes, password changes.

Read-only, and nothing new is recorded for it — `audit_events` has been
written all along and had no way out. Scoped like every other query, so a
project id that is not yours is a 404 rather than a confirmation that it
exists. Bounded, because an unlimited list is a way to read the whole table
in one request.

post.description:
Issue a key. The `key` field in this response is the only copy.

What is stored is `HMAC-SHA256(server_pepper, key)`. So a lost key cannot be
recovered -- only revoked and replaced -- and a stolen database cannot be
replayed against the API.

post.description:
Change your own password, without anyone touching the server.

There is no forgotten-password flow: that needs email, token storage and
expiry. The product says so where a user can read it rather than implying a
reset link exists. Until then a lockout is recovered by the owner running
`deploy/scripts/reset-password.sh`.

patch.description:
Adjust a draft version's presentation and custom fields.

Allowed only while the version is still a draft. Once it has passed a test
run, or a live key is pinned to it, a customer may be relying on the key
names it publishes — changing them would break their integration with no
signal — so from that point a change is a new version, and this returns
`409 schema_version_frozen` saying so.

post.description:
Score this version against documents already in the project.

For a template-only version this reuses the analysis extraction and costs
nothing: the analysis ran the whole template, so it already knows whether
each selected field was found.

A version with **custom fields** cannot be answered that way. The analysis
never looked for `site_ref`, so reporting "not found" would be reporting
that nobody asked — which is exactly the false reassurance a test run exists
to prevent. Those versions are therefore extracted for real, once per
document, and that does cost a model call. It is the honest price of the
question being asked.
